questions.question: Morning recess starts at 10:40 a.m. and lasts 25 minutes. What time does recess end?
questions.explain: From 10:40, 20 minutes takes you to 11:00, and 5 more minutes makes 11:05 a.m. The trap is writing 10:65 — once minutes reach 60 you must regroup them into a new hour.

questions.question: A ferry ride from Vancouver to Bowen Island lasts 1 h 40 min. How many minutes is that in total?
questions.explain: One hour is 60 minutes, so 60 + 40 = 100 minutes. The trap is just squashing the numbers together to get 140; an hour is 60 minutes, not 100.

questions.question: Nadia's soccer practice ended at 6:20 p.m. Practice lasted 45 minutes. What time did it start?
questions.explain: Go backwards: 20 minutes back from 6:20 is 6:00, and 25 more minutes back is 5:35 p.m. The trap is doing 45 − 20 = 25 and answering 5:25, or adding the 45 minutes instead of taking them away.

questions.question: Leo's ferry leaves Tsawwassen at 9:45 a.m. The crossing takes 1 h 35 min, and then his family drives 25 minutes to his grandma's house. What time do they arrive?
questions.explain: Add one step at a time: 9:45 + 1 h 35 min = 11:20 a.m., then + 25 min = 11:45 a.m. The trap is stopping at 11:20 and forgetting the second part of the journey.

questions.question: A junior hockey game in Kamloops starts at 10:50 a.m. and finishes at 1:05 p.m. How long does the game last?
questions.explain: Jump to a friendly time: 10:50 to 12:50 is 2 hours, then 12:50 to 1:05 is 15 minutes, so 2 h 15 min. The trap is counting the hour names 10 → 11 → 12 → 1 as 3 whole hours; the clock only starts at :50, not on the hour.

questions.question: Ella sees a full moon over Okanagan Lake on March 3. One full moon to the next takes about 29 days. About what date is the next full moon? (March has 31 days.)
questions.explain: March 3 plus 28 days lands on March 31, and one more day is April 1. The trap is treating every month as 30 days (3 + 29 = 32 → April 2); you must use the real number of days in March.

questions.question: At Kitsilano Beach the low tide is at 6:20 a.m. High tide comes about 6 h 15 min after low tide. About what time is high tide?
questions.explain: 6:20 a.m. plus 6 hours is 12:20 p.m. (you pass noon, so it becomes p.m.), and 15 more minutes gives 12:35 p.m. The trap is keeping a.m. after crossing 12:00 — 12:35 a.m. would be the middle of the night.

questions.question: A school concert in Victoria runs from 6:45 p.m. to 9:20 p.m. Jayden works it out as "9 − 6 = 3 hours and 45 − 20 = 25 minutes," so he answers 3 h 25 min. What is the actual duration of the concert?
questions.explain: Count forward instead: 6:45 to 9:00 is 2 h 15 min, and 9:00 to 9:20 is 20 min more, giving 2 h 35 min. Jayden's trap is stacking clock times like plain numbers — you can't subtract 20 − 45, so you must regroup 1 hour into 60 minutes.

questions.question: Amara's ferry to Nanaimo leaves at 11:05 a.m. She must be checked in 30 minutes before it leaves. The drive from her house to the terminal takes 1 h 20 min, and parking takes another 15 minutes before check-in. What is the latest time she can leave home?
questions.explain: Work backwards from 11:05: minus 30 min check-in = 10:35, minus 15 min parking = 10:20, minus 1 h 20 min driving = 9:00 a.m. The trap is leaving out one of the three steps — 9:30 is what you get if you forget the 30-minute check-in rule.

questions.question: In Prince George on December 21, the sun rises at 8:20 a.m. and sets at 3:50 p.m. On June 21, the sun rises at 5:00 a.m. and sets at 9:30 p.m. How much MORE daylight is there on June 21 than on December 21?
questions.explain: Find each daylight duration first: December is 8:20 a.m. to 3:50 p.m. = 7 h 30 min, June is 5:00 a.m. to 9:30 p.m. = 16 h 30 min, and 16 h 30 min − 7 h 30 min = 9 hours. The trap is answering with one of the day lengths (7 h 30 min or 16 h 30 min) instead of the difference between them.

questions.question: A ferry leaves Horseshoe Bay every 2 h 15 min, and the first sailing of the day is at 6:30 a.m. What time is the FOURTH sailing of the day?
questions.explain: The 1st sailing is 6:30 a.m., so there are only 3 gaps before the 4th: 8:45 a.m., 11:00 a.m., then 1:15 p.m. The trap is adding 2 h 15 min four times (which gives 3:30 p.m.) — the first sailing takes no waiting time at all.

questions.question: A silent reading block starts at 1:15 p.m. and ends at 2:00 p.m. How long does it last?
questions.explain: Count up from 1:15 to 2:00: that is 45 minutes. A common trap is doing 2 − 1 = 1 hour and then 15 more minutes to get 1 h 45 min — the hour is not finished yet, so you only count the minutes from 1:15 up to the next hour.

questions.question: One full day-and-night cycle is 24 hours. How many hours are in 3 days?
questions.explain: Multiply: 24 × 3 = 72 hours. The usual mistake is adding instead of multiplying and answering 27 hours — 3 days means three lots of 24 hours.

questions.question: Mira's piano lesson begins at 3:50 p.m. and lasts 40 minutes. What time does it end?
questions.explain: Jump 10 minutes to 4:00, then 30 more minutes to 4:30 p.m. The common trap is writing 3:50 + 40 as 3:90 and then trading 60 minutes for an hour but forgetting to move the hour forward, which gives 3:30.

questions.question: Kai's green bin is picked up every 14 days. The last pickup was May 6. What is the date of the next pickup?
questions.explain: Add the duration to the start date: 6 + 14 = 20, so the next pickup is May 20. A common slip is counting May 6 itself as day 1, which lands one day early on May 19.
